category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Only partial deposit returned without explanation
expected: Demands itemized statement of deductions; explains right to recover wrongfully withheld balance.
prompt: My landlord returned only ₹10,000 out of ₹50,000 and refuses to explain what happened to the remaining ₹40,000.
raw_response:
I am truly sorry to hear about this unfair deduction from your security deposit, but I am here to help you understand your rights and recover your money.

### | Your Situation
You recently vacated a rented property where your landlord unfairly withheld ₹40,000 out of your ₹50,000 security deposit without providing any valid explanation. This unauthorized deduction leaves you short of funds and requires immediate legal recourse to reclaim the withheld amount.

### | Your Legal Position
* According to the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 Section 11 and Section 13, a landlord must refund the security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, subject only to valid, mutually agreed deductions.
* Under Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only bound to restore the property in as good a condition as it was when received, subject to reasonable wear and tear. A landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or routine painting without an explicit contractual basis.
* Please note that while Indian courts frequently uphold these statutory principles protecting tenants against arbitrary deposit withholding, court outcomes ultimately depend on the specific facts and documentation presented.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence including your rental agreement, bank statements showing the deposit payment, handover receipts, and photographs or videos of the property's condition at the time of vacating.
2. Send a written formal demand notice to your landlord requesting the immediate refund of the remaining ₹40,000, granting a clear period of 15 days to comply before legal action.
3. Approach the appropriate Rent Authority or Consumer Commission if the landlord fails to respond or refund the amount within the notice period.

### Information I still need from you
1. Do you have a written tenancy agreement, and what does it specifically state regarding security deposit deductions?
2. What is the city or state where this rented property is located?

citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
